The files listed as untouched on purpose are not in the diff: VideoApp.tsx, ReadingApp.tsx, both LibraryFace.tsx, both shelfLinks.ts, both useDiscover.ts, backend/. frontend/src/lib/api.ts is also not changed; the spec says it changes only if needed, and the type already includes last_played.

The new code is only in the listed labels.ts files: ShelfSortChoice, CONTINUE_SORT_CHOICES and parseShelfSortId. SORT_CHOICES, SortChoice and parseSortId are left as they were, which matches item 1 of the spec.

VideoShelfPage.tsx:65-75 picks CONTINUE_SORT_CHOICES only when by === 'watch' && shelfKey === 'continue', and sets the selection again during render when the (by, key, initialSort) scope changes. The fetchPage memo at VideoShelfPage.tsx:103 depends on sort.sort and sort.order, so changing the choice requests the shelf again. This matches I1-I4 and I6 as read.
potential_unspecified_behavior: The selection scope includes initialSort, so a URL sort change on the same shelf page while it stays mounted also resets the selection to the URL's value. The spec only describes a by/key change. The UI does not change the URL sort on the shelf page (decisions.md: 'URL does not change'), so a user cannot normally reach this.
regression_risks: The shared sort menus SortChoiceMenu and ReadingSortMenu are now generic and take an optional choices prop that defaults to SORT_CHOICES. Library call sites pass no choices. The new I4 Library tests in both apps cover this, but I did not check every other caller of these menus.
test_coverage: Both new test files cover I1, I2 (the order of the five choices, each pair, choosing Last opened again), I3 (four valid ids, played, bogus, empty, null), I4 (four non-Continue shelves with sort=played, plus Library's menu) and I6 (leaving Continue, arriving at Continue, a URL sort kept across the change).
